items.title: Peter Vacher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001
items.q: there’s no question Humphrey Lyttelton has made an extraordinary impact.

ctx.x: Who in your estimation is the greatest, or most influential British jazz product?

It’s difficult to say isn’t it? Well for different reasons I guess, there’s no question Humphrey Lyttelton has made an extraordinary impact. Humph will be 80 this coming year. He’s had a band now for 50 years. Every British player of consequence has been in that band. Humph’s also been, he’s a Renaissance man, he’s presented a Monday night best of jazz radio program for 30 years. He’s written several excellent books, both an autobiography and of explanation of musical study. He’s an excellent trumpet player.

He’s composed probably a hundred or more original compositions. And he has probably the highest profile. He’s a most interesting character. He’s from a very privileged background. He’s an old Etonian, I mean Eton is our most prestigious public school, or you’d call it a private school. He comes from aristocratic stock and here was this extraordinary man who moved into a world of playing jazz music, which somehow was at odds with that kind of background. He was an officer of the guards during the war, which was…
